sources.effective_version: October 13 Chapter 447 was fully read on the General Court website, including 447:5, 6, 8, 9, 10, 12-a and 12-b. Its RSA index states current through the 2026 regular session, updated September 2026; official bound volumes were not read. Listed LSA links stop at 2023; no completed independent 2025-2026 bill search is claimed. Complete primary opinions were read: Boulia-Gorrell, 84 N.H. 174 (1929), Tolles-Bickford, 98 N.H. 55 (1953), and official In re McLaughlin, 2011 BNH 005. Boulia II supports one indivisible entire-contract lien preserved by furnishing within the historical 90-day attachment period; III discusses a possible separate extra-contract claim without deciding its facts. McLaughlin p6 describes 120 days after contractual completion, distinct from accrual; pp8-9 decide first-delivery priority while assuming perfection. Tolles rejects replacement-work and receivership extensions after contractual completion under historical 90 days. These reads supersede blanket case-unread/no-authority wording. CAP OCR confidence is 0.572 (Boulia) and 0.609 (Tolles); printed reporters, full historical amendments and current treatment remain unchecked. Contract identity, qualifying completion and attachment procedure remain qualified. October20 mandatory product correction supersedes the Series09 completion-based target: Yes to established entire contract retains first delivery +120 days, with no later last-delivery extension. This conservative product target does not resolve all doctrinal contract/perfection questions. Notice/account clocks,2026event window and pending approval remain unchanged; see the bound note and dated source observations.

October 13 complete Chapter 447 read and the General Court online compilation statement supersede the original access limitation. The website states currency through the 2026 regular session, updated September 2026, but identifies Thomson Reuters bound volumes/supplements as the official version. Specific procedure, interpretation and appointment limits remain.
Additional service, recording and amount conditions described below remain mandatory; this calculator is not a notice-sending or lien-filing service.

This is court attachment, not recorder filing. Start well before the target; RSA 511-A procedure remains unread. The October 13 reads include Boulia-Gorrell, 84 N.H. 174 (1929), describing an indivisible lien under one entire contract and whole-lien preservation within its historical 90-day period; McLaughlin, 2011 BNH 005, describes the 120-day completion clock but decides priority; Tolles-Bickford, 98 N.H. 55 (1953), rejects completed-contract replacement and receivership extensions. The retained first-delivery +120 date is a conservative review target, not a universal statutory expiration. Contract identity/completion, CAP reporter accuracy and current treatment remain qualified.

After the applicable owner notice, provide written accounts as often as once in thirty days. Late notice protects sums then due or that may thereafter become due to the contractor, agent or subcontractor. Unknown mortgage/posting facts require review; do not omit lender notice.

The General Court website states currency through the 2026 regular session, updated September 2026. Its displayed LSA links stop at 2023; no separate 2025–2026 bill/LSA search or bound official-edition review is recorded here. Retain the existing targeted election/Thanksgiving evidence and attachment-procedure limits.

preliminary_notice.name: Owner and construction lender notices
preliminary_notice.description: Lender notice is required within fifteen business days of the later trigger. Remote suppliers also notify owner BEFORE first delivery; retain both candidates.

lien_filing.name: Secure lien by writ of attachment
lien_filing.description: For the established entire-contract answer, use first qualifying delivery +120 days as the conservative lien-protection baseline required by the reviewed form. A later final delivery does not extend this target. Secure court attachment in time; notice coverage, amount, priority and attachment procedure still require their own facts.

preliminary_notice.name: Notice of intent before filing
preliminary_notice.description: No preliminary furnishing notice; intent is still mandatory at least thirty days before actual filing. Calculate the filing action target first, then subtract the full pre-filing notice interval; any notice-day adjustment moves earlier.

lien_filing.description: Six calendar months, clamping missing month-day as the approved earlier target. Filing must wait thirty days after actual intent service. Conservative action date shown; the statutory deadline remains unresolved. Obtain qualified review before this date.

sources.effective_version: October 13 Chapter 447 was fully read on the General Court website, including 447:5, 6, 8, 9, 10, 12-a and 12-b. Its RSA index states current through the 2026 regular session, updated September 2026; official bound volumes were not read. Listed LSA links stop at 2023; no completed independent 2025-2026 bill search is claimed. Complete primary opinions were read: Boulia-Gorrell, 84 N.H. 174 (1929), Tolles-Bickford, 98 N.H. 55 (1953), and official In re McLaughlin, 2011 BNH 005. Boulia II supports one indivisible entire-contract lien preserved by furnishing within the historical 90-day attachment period; III discusses a possible separate extra-contract claim without deciding its facts. McLaughlin p6 describes 120 days after contractual completion, distinct from accrual; pp8-9 decide first-delivery priority while assuming perfection. Tolles rejects replacement-work and receivership extensions after contractual completion under historical 90 days. These reads supersede blanket case-unread/no-authority wording. CAP OCR confidence is 0.572 (Boulia) and 0.609 (Tolles); printed reporters, full historical amendments and current treatment remain unchecked. Contract identity, qualifying completion and attachment procedure remain qualified. October20 mandatory product correction supersedes the Series09 completion-based target: Yes to established entire contract retains first delivery +120 days, with no later last-delivery extension. This conservative product target does not resolve all doctrinal contract/perfection questions. Notice/account clocks,2026event window and pending approval remain unchanged; see the bound note and dated source observations.

Additional service, recording and amount conditions described below remain mandatory; this calculator is not a notice-sending or lien-filing service.

This is court attachment, not recorder filing. Start well before the target; RSA 511-A procedure remains unread. The October 13 reads include Boulia-Gorrell, 84 N.H. 174 (1929), describing an indivisible lien under one entire contract and whole-lien preservation within its historical 90-day period; McLaughlin, 2011 BNH 005, describes the 120-day completion clock but decides priority; Tolles-Bickford, 98 N.H. 55 (1953), rejects completed-contract replacement and receivership extensions. The retained first-delivery +120 date is a conservative review target, not a universal statutory expiration. Contract identity/completion, CAP reporter accuracy and current treatment remain qualified.

After the applicable owner notice, provide written accounts as often as once in thirty days. Late notice protects sums then due or that may thereafter become due to the contractor, agent or subcontractor. Unknown mortgage/posting facts require review; do not omit lender notice.

recurring_notice_intake.label: Actual owner notice and written accounts
recurring_notice_intake.help: Enter actual written accounts and establish the separate actual owner notice. The latest actual act plus thirty days is an advisory checkpoint only; later accounts do not establish timely earlier coverage or a legal cadence reset.

preliminary_notice.name: Owner and construction lender notices
preliminary_notice.description: Lender notice is required within fifteen business days of the later trigger. Remote suppliers also notify owner BEFORE first delivery; retain both candidates.

notice_duties.name: Owner notice before furnishing
notice_duties.description: Give written notice to the owner or person having charge of the property before first furnishing. A later notice has the unpaid-balance limitations in RSA 447:6; preserve the existing late-notice and balance review path.

notice_duties.name: Construction lender notice
notice_duties.description: Provide written notice to the institution providing the construction funds within fifteen business days of the later of first furnishing or the actual jobsite lender posting. Include the name and address of the jobsite. Failure to provide this notice alone does not invalidate the lien (RSA 447:12-b(II)); preserve the bound service and business-day rules.

lien_filing.name: Secure lien by writ of attachment
lien_filing.description: For the established entire-contract answer, use first qualifying delivery +120 days as the conservative lien-protection baseline required by the reviewed form. A later final delivery does not extend this target. Secure court attachment in time; notice coverage, amount, priority and attachment procedure still require their own facts.

sources.effective_version: October 13 Chapter 447 was fully read on the General Court website, including 447:5, 6, 8, 9, 10, 12-a and 12-b. Its RSA index states current through the 2026 regular session, updated September 2026; official bound volumes were not read. Listed LSA links stop at 2023; no completed independent 2025-2026 bill search is claimed. Complete primary opinions were read: Boulia-Gorrell, 84 N.H. 174 (1929), Tolles-Bickford, 98 N.H. 55 (1953), and official In re McLaughlin, 2011 BNH 005. Boulia II supports one indivisible entire-contract lien preserved by furnishing within the historical 90-day attachment period; III discusses a possible separate extra-contract claim without deciding its facts. McLaughlin p6 describes 120 days after contractual completion, distinct from accrual; pp8-9 decide first-delivery priority while assuming perfection. Tolles rejects replacement-work and receivership extensions after contractual completion under historical 90 days. These reads supersede blanket case-unread/no-authority wording. CAP OCR confidence is 0.572 (Boulia) and 0.609 (Tolles); printed reporters, full historical amendments and current treatment remain unchecked. Contract identity, qualifying completion and attachment procedure remain qualified. October20 mandatory product correction supersedes the Series09 completion-based target: Yes to established entire contract retains first delivery +120 days, with no later last-delivery extension. This conservative product target does not resolve all doctrinal contract/perfection questions. Notice/account clocks,2026event window and pending approval remain unchanged; see the bound note and dated source observations.

The website states currency through the 2026 regular session, updated September 2026, but identifies Thomson Reuters bound volumes/supplements as the official version. Specific procedure, interpretation and appointment limits remain.
Additional service, recording and amount conditions described below remain mandatory; this calculator is not a notice-sending or lien-filing service.

This is court attachment, not recorder filing. Start well before the target; RSA 511-A procedure remains unread. The October 13 reads include Boulia-Gorrell, 84 N.H. 174 (1929), describing an indivisible lien under one entire contract and whole-lien preservation within its historical 90-day period; McLaughlin, 2011 BNH 005, describes the 120-day completion clock but decides priority; Tolles-Bickford, 98 N.H. 55 (1953), rejects completed-contract replacement and receivership extensions. The retained first-delivery +120 date is a conservative review target, not a universal statutory expiration. Contract identity/completion, CAP reporter accuracy and current treatment remain qualified.

After the applicable owner notice, provide written accounts as often as once in thirty days. Late notice protects sums then due or that may thereafter become due to the contractor, agent or subcontractor. Unknown mortgage/posting facts require review; do not omit lender notice.

The General Court website states currency through the 2026 regular session, updated September 2026. Its displayed LSA links stop at 2023; no separate 2025–2026 bill/LSA search or bound official-edition review is recorded here. Retain the existing targeted election/Thanksgiving evidence and attachment-procedure limits.

recurring_notice_intake.label: Actual owner notice and written accounts
recurring_notice_intake.help: Enter actual written accounts and establish the separate actual owner notice. The latest actual act plus thirty days is an advisory checkpoint only; later accounts do not establish timely earlier coverage or a legal cadence reset.

preliminary_notice.name: Owner and construction lender notices
preliminary_notice.description: Lender notice is required within fifteen business days of the later trigger. Remote suppliers also notify owner BEFORE first delivery; retain both candidates.

notice_duties.name: Owner notice before furnishing
notice_duties.description: Give written notice to the owner or person having charge of the property before first furnishing. A later notice has the unpaid-balance limitations in RSA 447:6; preserve the existing late-notice and balance review path.

notice_duties.name: Construction lender notice
notice_duties.description: Provide written notice to the institution providing the construction funds within fifteen business days of the later of first furnishing or the actual jobsite lender posting. Include the name and address of the jobsite. Failure to provide this notice alone does not invalidate the lien (RSA 447:12-b(II)); preserve the bound service and business-day rules.

lien_filing.name: Secure lien by writ of attachment
lien_filing.description: For the established entire-contract answer, use first qualifying delivery +120 days as the conservative lien-protection baseline required by the reviewed form. A later final delivery does not extend this target. Secure court attachment in time; notice coverage, amount, priority and attachment procedure still require their own facts.

preliminary_notice.name: Applicable furnishing and formal intent notices
preliminary_notice.description: File directory Notice of Furnishing within forty-five days of first delivery, including direct owner suppliers. Remote suppliers also give formal intent at least thirty days BEFORE the conservative claim filing date.

notice_duties.name: Directory Notice of Furnishing
notice_duties.description: File a Notice of Furnishing in the directory within forty-five days after first furnishing for the established searchable project with a filed and posted Notice of Commencement. The formal preclaim notice to the owner is separate.

planned_notice_targets.name: Thirty-day formal intent planning target
planned_notice_targets.description: This target assumes filing on the stated earlier filing date. Give the owner formal written notice of intent at least thirty days before actual filing; earlier actual filing requires an earlier notice. This planning target is not a universal statutory expiration and does not establish legally sufficient service.

lien_filing.name: File claim with prothonotary

questions.label: Was the required mailing completed within 200 days of your first delivery?
questions.help: Confirm the notice was mailed to the required recipient before or within 200 calendar days after first qualifying delivery, using the required method. Recording and mailing have independent limits. No or Unknown requires review; timely recording alone cannot prove timely mailing.

questions.label: When was the notice recorded (and mailed, if the same day)?
questions.help: The forty-day clock starts on actual recording, even when mailing is outstanding or occurred on a different day. Do not substitute the later mailing date.

sources.effective_version: October 13 Chapter 447 was fully read on the General Court website, including 447:5, 6, 8, 9, 10, 12-a and 12-b. Its RSA index states current through the 2026 regular session, updated September 2026; official bound volumes were not read. Listed LSA links stop at 2023; no completed independent 2025-2026 bill search is claimed. Complete primary opinions were read: Boulia-Gorrell, 84 N.H. 174 (1929), Tolles-Bickford, 98 N.H. 55 (1953), and official In re McLaughlin, 2011 BNH 005. Boulia II supports one indivisible entire-contract lien preserved by furnishing within the historical 90-day attachment period; III discusses a possible separate extra-contract claim without deciding its facts. McLaughlin p6 describes 120 days after contractual completion, distinct from accrual; pp8-9 decide first-delivery priority while assuming perfection. Tolles rejects replacement-work and receivership extensions after contractual completion under historical 90 days. These reads supersede blanket case-unread/no-authority wording. CAP OCR confidence is 0.572 (Boulia) and 0.609 (Tolles); printed reporters, full historical amendments and current treatment remain unchecked. Contract identity, qualifying completion and attachment procedure remain qualified. October20 mandatory product correction supersedes the Series09 completion-based target: Yes to established entire contract retains first delivery +120 days, with no later last-delivery extension. This conservative product target does not resolve all doctrinal contract/perfection questions. Notice/account clocks,2026event window and pending approval remain unchanged; see the bound note and dated source observations.

preliminary_notice.name: Prime notice and intent notice
preliminary_notice.description: Serve prime notice within ten days and intent at least thirty days before actual filing; both apply. Calculate the filing action target first, then subtract the full pre-filing notice interval; any notice-day adjustment moves earlier.

notice_duties.name: Ten-day prime notice
notice_duties.description: With own subcontractors or suppliers and no written owner contract, serve the separate prime notice on the owner or authorized agent within ten days after first furnishing. The later notice of intent is separate.

planned_notice_targets.name: Thirty-day owner intent planning target
planned_notice_targets.description: This target assumes filing on the stated earlier filing date. Serve the owner notice of intent at least thirty days before actual filing; earlier actual filing requires an earlier notice. This planning target is not a universal statutory expiration and does not establish service or receipt.

lien_filing.name: File claim with circuit court clerk
lien_filing.description: Six calendar months, clamping missing month-day as the approved earlier target. Filing must wait thirty days after actual intent service. Conservative action date shown; the statutory deadline remains unresolved. Obtain qualified review before this date.

sources.effective_version: October 13 Chapter 447 was fully read on the General Court website, including 447:5, 6, 8, 9, 10, 12-a and 12-b. Its RSA index states current through the 2026 regular session, updated September 2026; official bound volumes were not read. Listed LSA links stop at 2023; no completed independent 2025-2026 bill search is claimed. Complete primary opinions were read: Boulia-Gorrell, 84 N.H. 174 (1929), Tolles-Bickford, 98 N.H. 55 (1953), and official In re McLaughlin, 2011 BNH 005. Boulia II supports one indivisible entire-contract lien preserved by furnishing within the historical 90-day attachment period; III discusses a possible separate extra-contract claim without deciding its facts. McLaughlin p6 describes 120 days after contractual completion, distinct from accrual; pp8-9 decide first-delivery priority while assuming perfection. Tolles rejects replacement-work and receivership extensions after contractual completion under historical 90 days. These reads supersede blanket case-unread/no-authority wording. CAP OCR confidence is 0.572 (Boulia) and 0.609 (Tolles); printed reporters, full historical amendments and current treatment remain unchecked. Contract identity, qualifying completion and attachment procedure remain qualified. October20 mandatory product correction supersedes the Series09 completion-based target: Yes to established entire contract retains first delivery +120 days, with no later last-delivery extension. This conservative product target does not resolve all doctrinal contract/perfection questions. Notice/account clocks,2026event window and pending approval remain unchanged; see the bound note and dated source observations.

This is court attachment, not recorder filing. Start well before the target; RSA 511-A procedure remains unread. The October 13 reads include Boulia-Gorrell, 84 N.H. 174 (1929), describing an indivisible lien under one entire contract and whole-lien preservation within its historical 90-day period; McLaughlin, 2011 BNH 005, describes the 120-day completion clock but decides priority; Tolles-Bickford, 98 N.H. 55 (1953), rejects completed-contract replacement and receivership extensions. The retained first-delivery +120 date is a conservative review target, not a universal statutory expiration. Contract identity/completion, CAP reporter accuracy and current treatment remain qualified.

After the applicable owner notice, provide written accounts as often as once in thirty days. Late notice protects sums then due or that may thereafter become due to the contractor, agent or subcontractor. Unknown mortgage/posting facts require review; do not omit lender notice.

recurring_notice_intake.label: Actual owner notice and written accounts
recurring_notice_intake.help: Enter actual written accounts and establish the separate actual owner notice. The latest actual act plus thirty days is an advisory checkpoint only; later accounts do not establish timely earlier coverage or a legal cadence reset.

preliminary_notice.name: Owner and construction lender notices
preliminary_notice.description: Lender notice is required within fifteen business days of the later trigger. Remote suppliers also notify owner BEFORE first delivery; retain both candidates.

notice_duties.name: Owner notice before furnishing
notice_duties.description: Give written notice to the owner or person having charge of the property before first furnishing. A later notice has the unpaid-balance limitations in RSA 447:6; preserve the existing late-notice and balance review path.

notice_duties.name: Construction lender notice
notice_duties.description: Provide written notice to the institution providing the construction funds within fifteen business days of the later of first furnishing or the actual jobsite lender posting. Include the name and address of the jobsite. Failure to provide this notice alone does not invalidate the lien (RSA 447:12-b(II)); preserve the bound service and business-day rules.

lien_filing.name: Secure lien by writ of attachment
lien_filing.description: For the established entire-contract answer, use first qualifying delivery +120 days as the conservative lien-protection baseline required by the reviewed form. A later final delivery does not extend this target. Secure court attachment in time; notice coverage, amount, priority and attachment procedure still require their own facts.

preliminary_notice.name: 60-day supplier notice and 30-day intent
preliminary_notice.description: Serve two signed copies of supplier notice on owner/agent; separately serve intent at least thirty days before actual filing. Calculate the filing action target first, then subtract the full pre-filing notice interval; any notice-day adjustment moves earlier.

notice_duties.name: Sixty-day supplier notice
notice_duties.description: Serve the statutory supplier notice in two signed copies on the owner or authorized agent within sixty days after first furnishing. The later notice of intent is separate; this date does not establish service or receipt.

planned_notice_targets.name: Thirty-day owner intent planning target
planned_notice_targets.description: This target assumes filing on the stated earlier filing date. Serve the owner notice of intent at least thirty days before actual filing; earlier actual filing requires an earlier notice. This planning target is not a universal statutory expiration and does not establish service or receipt.

lien_filing.name: File claim with circuit court clerk
lien_filing.description: Six calendar months, clamping missing month-day as the approved earlier target. Filing must wait thirty days after actual intent service. Conservative action date shown; the statutory deadline remains unresolved. Obtain qualified review before this date.

preliminary_notice.name: 60-day supplier notice and 30-day intent
preliminary_notice.description: Serve two signed copies of supplier notice on owner/agent; separately serve intent at least thirty days before actual filing. Calculate the filing action target first, then subtract the full pre-filing notice interval; any notice-day adjustment moves earlier.

notice_duties.name: Sixty-day supplier notice
notice_duties.description: Serve the statutory supplier notice in two signed copies on the owner or authorized agent within sixty days after first furnishing. The later notice of intent is separate; this date does not establish service or receipt.

planned_notice_targets.name: Thirty-day owner intent planning target
planned_notice_targets.description: This target assumes filing on the stated earlier filing date. Serve the owner notice of intent at least thirty days before actual filing; earlier actual filing requires an earlier notice. This planning target is not a universal statutory expiration and does not establish service or receipt.

lien_filing.name: File claim with circuit court clerk
lien_filing.description: Six calendar months, clamping missing month-day as the approved earlier target. Filing must wait thirty days after actual intent service. Conservative action date shown; the statutory deadline remains unresolved. Obtain qualified review before this date.

sources.effective_version: October 13 Chapter 447 was fully read on the General Court website, including 447:5, 6, 8, 9, 10, 12-a and 12-b. Its RSA index states current through the 2026 regular session, updated September 2026; official bound volumes were not read. Listed LSA links stop at 2023; no completed independent 2025-2026 bill search is claimed. Complete primary opinions were read: Boulia-Gorrell, 84 N.H. 174 (1929), Tolles-Bickford, 98 N.H. 55 (1953), and official In re McLaughlin, 2011 BNH 005. Boulia II supports one indivisible entire-contract lien preserved by furnishing within the historical 90-day attachment period; III discusses a possible separate extra-contract claim without deciding its facts. McLaughlin p6 describes 120 days after contractual completion, distinct from accrual; pp8-9 decide first-delivery priority while assuming perfection. Tolles rejects replacement-work and receivership extensions after contractual completion under historical 90 days. These reads supersede blanket case-unread/no-authority wording. CAP OCR confidence is 0.572 (Boulia) and 0.609 (Tolles); printed reporters, full historical amendments and current treatment remain unchecked. Contract identity, qualifying completion and attachment procedure remain qualified. October20 mandatory product correction supersedes the Series09 completion-based target: Yes to established entire contract retains first delivery +120 days, with no later last-delivery extension. This conservative product target does not resolve all doctrinal contract/perfection questions. Notice/account clocks,2026event window and pending approval remain unchanged; see the bound note and dated source observations.

The October 13 reads include Boulia-Gorrell, 84 N.H. 174 (1929), describing an indivisible lien under one entire contract and whole-lien preservation within its historical 90-day period; McLaughlin, 2011 BNH 005, describes the 120-day completion clock but decides priority; Tolles-Bickford, 98 N.H. 55 (1953), rejects completed-contract replacement and receivership extensions. The retained first-delivery +120 date is a conservative review target, not a universal statutory expiration. Contract identity/completion, CAP reporter accuracy and current treatment remain qualified.

After the applicable owner notice, provide written accounts as often as once in thirty days. Late notice protects sums then due or that may thereafter become due to the contractor, agent or subcontractor. Unknown mortgage/posting facts require review; do not omit lender notice.

recurring_notice_intake.label: Actual owner notice and written accounts
recurring_notice_intake.help: Enter actual written accounts and establish the separate actual owner notice. The latest actual act plus thirty days is an advisory checkpoint only; later accounts do not establish timely earlier coverage or a legal cadence reset.

preliminary_notice.name: Owner and construction lender notices
preliminary_notice.description: Lender notice is required within fifteen business days of the later trigger. Remote suppliers also notify owner BEFORE first delivery; retain both candidates.

notice_duties.name: Owner notice before furnishing
notice_duties.description: Give written notice to the owner or person having charge of the property before first furnishing. A later notice has the unpaid-balance limitations in RSA 447:6; preserve the existing late-notice and balance review path.

notice_duties.name: Construction lender notice
notice_duties.description: Provide written notice to the institution providing the construction funds within fifteen business days of the later of first furnishing or the actual jobsite lender posting. Include the name and address of the jobsite. Failure to provide this notice alone does not invalidate the lien (RSA 447:12-b(II)); preserve the bound service and business-day rules.

lien_filing.name: Secure lien by writ of attachment
lien_filing.description: For the established entire-contract answer, use first qualifying delivery +120 days as the conservative lien-protection baseline required by the reviewed form. A later final delivery does not extend this target. Secure court attachment in time; notice coverage, amount, priority and attachment procedure still require their own facts.

notice_duties.description: Serve the statutory supplier notice in two signed copies on the owner or authorized agent within sixty days after first furnishing. The later notice of intent is separate; this date does not establish service or receipt.

planned_notice_targets.name: Thirty-day owner intent planning target
planned_notice_targets.description: This target assumes filing on the stated earlier filing date. Serve the owner notice of intent at least thirty days before actual filing; earlier actual filing requires an earlier notice. This planning target is not a universal statutory expiration and does not establish service or receipt.

lien_filing.name: File claim with circuit court clerk
lien_filing.description: Six calendar months, clamping missing month-day as the approved earlier target. Filing must wait thirty days after actual intent service. Conservative action date shown; the statutory deadline remains unresolved. Obtain qualified review before this date.
